userStories.title: Protect nax config files in the raw Bash screen
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deny parseable raw Bash tokens and redirects that name nax configuration files before the production resolver can hide them.

**Motivation** — Under the shipped default `bashApproval: raw`, `screenRawBashCommand` (`src/tools/policy-bash-raw.ts`) is the only thing between an agent mistake and nax's own run configuration.

**Approach** — `protectedHit` keeps its loop over every live frame in `cwd`, but checks nax config files **before and independently of** `args.resolvePath`:

1. For each `directory` in `cwd`, compute the lexical candidate
   `realOrRaw(resolve(directory, candidate))` (`realOrRaw` from `src/utils/realpath.ts` resolves
   the nearest existing ancestor, so a not-yet-created file under a symlinked temp root still
   compares equal to `realOrRaw(root)`).
2. If `isNaxConfigFile(args.root, lexical)` is true, return `candidate` (a hit).
3. Otherwise continue exactly as today: `args.resolvePath(candidate, directory)`, `continue` on
   `null`, then the `isNaxOwnedWritePath` check on the root-relative path.

`resolveWithin` is not changed: typed tools (Read, Grep, Write, Edit, ...) must keep receiving
`null` for these files. The fix lives entirely in `src/tools/policy-bash-raw.ts`;
`src/tools/policy.ts` is 587 lines against the 600-line source limit and gains nothing.

The screen denies any parseable token or redirect that names a nax config file, not only
writes; that is the screen's existing contract for every protected path and is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: lexical config-file detection in the raw Bash screen and focused unit/production-entry regression coverage. Out: remembered-approval commit recording and gated/escalate inert-stage warnings; `resolveWithin` in `src/tools/policy.ts` is not modified; typed tools must keep receiving `null` for nax config files; the raw screen does not gain `.git/` protection or any containment check; `raw` enforces no root containment by design; and commands the lexer refuses (substitution, heredocs, backticks) stay unscreened; the screen is an advisory mistake-catcher, and the OS sandbox is what makes the guarantee airtight.

**Interface**
```typescript
screenRawBashCommand(args: RawScreenArgs): BashCheck
isNaxConfigFile(root: string, resolved: string): boolean
resolveWithin(root: string, candidate: string): string | null
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given bashApproval `raw` and a pre-written root `.nax/config.json`, when `runtime.callTool("Bash", { command: "echo x > .nax/config.json" })` is invoked on support returned by `resolveCodingToolSupport`, then it returns `kind: "denied"`.
Given the denied root-config Bash call, when the bytes of `.nax/config.json` are read afterward, then they equal the bytes written before the call.

Given a pre-written `.nax/mono/packages/app/config.json`, when `runtime.callTool("Bash", { command: "echo x > .nax/mono/packages/app/config.json" })` is invoked through the production entry, then it returns `kind: "denied"`.
Given the denied mono-config Bash call, when the bytes of `.nax/mono/packages/app/config.json` are read afterward, then they are unchanged.
When `callTool("Bash", { command: "touch .nax/config.json" })` is invoked through the same production entry, then it returns `kind: "denied"`.
When `callTool("Bash", { command: "echo x > .nax/features/f1/prd.json" })` is invoked through the same production entry, then it still returns `kind: "denied"`.
When `callTool("Bash", { command: "echo hi > ../outside.txt" })` is invoked through the same production entry, then it is not denied by the screen, so raw mode still enforces no containment.
When `callTool("Bash", { command: "echo ok > notes.txt" })` is invoked through the same production entry, then it returns `kind: "ok"`.
When `resolveWithin(root, join(root, ".nax", "config.json"))` is called, then it still returns `null`.
Given a `screenRawBashCommand` resolver that returns `null` for every candidate, when screening `echo x > .nax/config.json`, then it denies with a reason naming `.nax/config.json`.

routing.reasoning: The change is a local policy-ordering correction, but it needs direct and production-entry filesystem regressions across existing resolver seams.

modifiedFiles.reason: may gain cases for the root nax config file and a per-package mono config file; its existing assertions stay valid and must not be weakened.

userStories.title: Record the build commit on remembered approvals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist `NAX_COMMIT` rather than an unset environment variable when a human remembers an escalated Bash approval.

**Motivation** — Every entry in `approvals.json` is therefore untraceable to the build that asked for it.

**Approach** — `onRemember` in `executionStage.execute` writes `naxCommit: NAX_COMMIT` (imported from
`@/version`) instead of reading `process.env.NAX_COMMIT`. To make the callback reachable from a
test without driving a real Telegram approval, `createHumanAskLink` is added to the existing
`_executionDeps` object in `src/pipeline/stages/execution.ts`, and the stage calls it through
`_executionDeps.createHumanAskLink` so a test can capture the options it receives.

**Scope** — In: execution-stage dependency injection and remembered approval provenance, with persisted-store coverage. Out: raw protected-path screening and inert Bash-stage warnings; approval-cache matching, interaction transport, audit `approval.remembered`, and historic approvals migration.

**Interface**
```typescript
createHumanAskLink(opts: { chain, timeoutMs, featureName?, storyId?, onRemember?, abortSignal? }): HumanAskLink
NAX_COMMIT: string
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `process.env.NAX_COMMIT` is unset, when the `onRemember` callback captured from `_executionDeps.createHumanAskLink` during `executionStage.execute` is invoked, then it appends an entry to `approvalsPath(ctx.runtime.outputDir)` whose `naxCommit` equals `NAX_COMMIT` from `@/version`.
Given `NAX_COMMIT` is not `"unknown"`, when the captured `onRemember` callback appends its approval entry, then that entry's `naxCommit` is not the string `"unknown"`.
When the captured `onRemember` callback receives an `AskRequest`, then its appended approval entry carries `origin: "escalate"` and the request's `command`.

routing.reasoning: An existing callback receives one injected factory seam and replaces one persisted field source with the already exported build constant.

userStories.title: Warn when gated or escalate stages cannot offer Bash
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Detect Bash-declaring stages whose resolved gated/escalate permissions contain no Bash grant, warn once per inert stage at run start, and document the required allow rule.

**Motivation** — Under `gated`/`escalate` a stage is offered Bash only when its resolved grants already contain a `Bash` entry, which comes solely from a human-written `Bash(...)` allow rule.

**Approach** — Detection is a pure function in a new module `src/config/inert-bash-stages.ts`, re-exported
from the `src/config` barrel:

```ts
import type { PipelineStage } from "./permissions";
import type { NaxConfig } from "./runtime-types";

/** Stages that dispatch at least one operation declaring the Bash tool. */
export const BASH_DECLARING_STAGES: readonly PipelineStage[] = ["run", "review", "rectification", "acceptance"];

/** Stages whose resolved bashApproval is gated/escalate AND whose resolved grants hold no Bash entry. */
export function findInertBashStages(config: NaxConfig): readonly PipelineStage[];
```

Logging follows the existing run-setup warning precedent: `warnFallbackMisconfiguration(config,
agentGetFn, logger)` in `src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-warnings.ts`, called directly from
`setupRun`. A sibling `warnInertBashStages(config: NaxConfig, logger: ReturnType<typeof getSafeLogger>): void`
goes in that same file and logs one warning per stage `findInertBashStages` returns.

`findInertBashStages` decides from `resolvePermissions(config, stage)` alone: the stage is inert
when the returned `bashApproval` is `"gated"` or `"escalate"` and no entry of `toolGrants` has
`tool === "Bash"`. An absent `toolGrants` counts as an empty list: the fail-closed branch for an
unrecognised `permissionProfile` returns `{ mode, bashApproval: "gated" }` with no `toolGrants`
field (`src/config/permissions.ts:281-282`). That is the same grant list `resolveBashSupport` searches, so the warning and
the tool offer cannot disagree. `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES` mirrors the `stage` field of the nine
operations that declare `Bash`: `implementerOp`, `testWriterOp` (`run`); `rectifyOp` (`review`);
`fullSuiteRectifyOp`, `finishFixOp`, `implementerRectifyOp`, `testWriterRectifyOp`
(`rectification`); `acceptanceFixSourceOp`, `acceptanceFixTestOp` (`acceptance`).

The warning is logged with stage `"permissions"`, and its message names the stage, the mode and
the fix, e.g.
`bashApproval "escalate" on stage "run" grants no Bash (no Bash(...) allow rule) -- the agent is not offered Bash, so nothing can escalate. Add one rule: "allow": ["Bash(ls *, cat *, git status*)"]`.
Its data object carries `{ storyId: "_setup", stage, bashApproval }`, matching the sibling
`warnFallbackMisconfiguration` warning's `storyId: "_setup"`. It is a warning, never an error: `gated`
without a rule is a legitimate "no shell" posture.

`setupRun` (`src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts`) calls `warnInertBashStages(options.config,
logger)` once, next to its existing `warnFallbackMisconfiguration` call.

Documentation, same story:

- `docs/adr/ADR-030-bash-approval-modes.md` — the mode table's `gated` and `escalate` rows state
  that Bash is offered only where a `Bash(...)` allow rule resolves for the stage, with a
  single-expression example `"allow": ["Bash(ls *, cat *, git status*)"]`, and that one
  expression per stage is required (a second `Bash(...)` entry is a config load error).
- `src/config/schemas-execution.ts` — a docblock on the `bashApproval` field stating the same
  requirement with the same example.
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-p2-interactive-approval-gate-design.md` §9 — the exit
  instruction to set `bashApproval: escalate` also adds the `Bash(...)` allow rule.

**Scope** — In: the pure resolved-permission detector, config-barrel exports, startup warnings, and the specified docs/schema comments. Out: raw-screen protection and approval commit recording; nax#2194 (under `escalate`, Category B checks are skipped for ungranted or unlexable Bash commands) is not part of this feature; `checkBashCommand`'s evaluation order is unchanged; the warning reads the root run config only; per-package `.nax/mono/<pkg>/config.json` overrides of `bashApproval` or permissions are not inspected; op-level `toolPatterns` narrowing is not considered; a stage is inert only when its resolved grants contain no `Bash` entry at all; and an inert stage is never turned into a config error or a run failure.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const BASH_DECLARING_STAGES: readonly PipelineStage[] = ["run", "review", "rectification", "acceptance"];
export function findInertBashStages(config: NaxConfig): readonly PipelineStage[];
warnInertBashStages(config: NaxConfig, logger: ReturnType<typeof getSafeLogger>): void
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given a config with `bashApproval: "escalate"`, `permissionProfile: "unrestricted"`, and no `permissions` block, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it returns every entry of `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES`.
Given a config with `bashApproval: "escalate"` and `permissions.run.allow` set to `["Bash(ls *)"]`, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then its result does not include `"run"`.
Given a config with `bashApproval: "gated"` and no `Bash(...)` rule, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it returns every entry of `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES`.
Given a config with `bashApproval: "raw"`, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it returns an empty list.
Given global `bashApproval: "raw"` and `permissions.review.bashApproval: "escalate"` with no `Bash(...)` rule, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it returns exactly `["review"]`.
Given a gated config with no `Bash(...)` rule, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it never returns a stage outside `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES`, including `"plan"` and `"verify"`.

Given `bashApproval: "escalate"` and `permissions.run.allow` set to `["Bash(ls *)"]`, when `resolveBashSupport` receives `declared: ["Bash"]` and grants returned by `resolvePermissions(config, "run")`, then it yields `allowBash: true` with a Bash grant present, agreeing with `findInertBashStages` excluding `"run"`.
Given a config whose `permissionProfile` is outside the schema enum, when `findInertBashStages` is called, then it returns every entry of `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES` without throwing.

When the stages of `implementerOp`, `testWriterOp`, `rectifyOp`, `fullSuiteRectifyOp`, `finishFixOp`, `implementerRectifyOp`, `testWriterRectifyOp`, `acceptanceFixSourceOp`, and `acceptanceFixTestOp` are examined, then each is an entry of `BASH_DECLARING_STAGES`.

Given an escalate config with `permissions.run.allow` set to `["Bash(ls *)"]` and a spy logger, when `warnInertBashStages` is called, then its warn calls are exactly three calls with stage `"permissions"`, one each for `"review"`, `"rectification"`, and `"acceptance"`.
When `warnInertBashStages` logs an inert stage for that escalate config, then each warning data object carries `storyId: "_setup"`, the inert `stage`, and `bashApproval: "escalate"`.
When `warnInertBashStages` logs an inert stage, then each warning message contains `Bash(`, naming the rule that would fix it.
Given a raw config and a spy logger, when `warnInertBashStages` is called, then it never calls `warn`.

Given a config of `bashApproval: "escalate"` with no `Bash(...)` rule, when the real `setupRun` is driven under `withWarnSpy`, then it logs a warning with stage `"permissions"` whose data object carries `stage: "run"`.
Given a config of `bashApproval: "raw"`, when the real `setupRun` is driven under `withWarnSpy`, then it logs no warning with stage `"permissions"` whose data object carries a `bashApproval` field.

routing.reasoning: This adds a new configuration abstraction that must stay aligned with grant resolution and integrates it through a startup logging seam, barrel exports, documentation, and unit plus real setup tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: the barrel must re-export BASH_DECLARING_STAGES and findInertBashStages so the run-setup warnings module imports them through the config barrel.
gains `warnInertBashStages(config, logger)` beside `warnFallbackMisconfiguration`; existing warnings are unchanged.

the `bashApproval` field gains a docblock stating that under `gated` and `escalate` Bash is offered only where a single `Bash(...)` allow expression resolves for the stage, with the example `"allow": ["Bash(ls *, cat *, git status*)"]`; no schema behaviour changes.

the mode table's `gated` and `escalate` rows must state that Bash is offered only where a `Bash(...)` allow rule resolves for the stage, give the single-expression example, and note that a second `Bash(...)` entry in one list is a config load error.
§9's instruction to set `bashApproval: escalate` on the P0 baseline corpora must also add the `Bash(...)` allow rule, or the exit run sends no prompts.

analysis:
This feature changes three established TypeScript seams and needs no config migration. Raw Bash screening is isolated in `src/tools/policy-bash-raw.ts`: `protectedHit` currently calls `args.resolvePath` before `isNaxConfigFile` and skips null results (`src/tools/policy-bash-raw.ts:78-87`). The production resolver is `resolveWithin(resolvedRoot, resolve(cwd, candidate))` (`src/tools/policy.ts:577`), while `isNaxConfigFile` already uses `realOrRaw(root)` and recognizes the root and nested mono config forms (`src/tools/nax-owned-writes.ts:17-43`). The correction belongs only in the raw screen: import and apply `resolve`/`realOrRaw` to every live cwd frame before the existing resolver path, retaining existing null handling and root-relative `isNaxOwnedWritePath` behavior. Do not alter `resolveWithin`, because typed tools rely on its null result for these files. Regression risk is accidentally gating raw outside-root paths or lexer-refused commands; production-entry tests must preserve raw pass-through as well as direct screen tests.

Execution directly calls imported `createHumanAskLink` and persists `process.env.NAX_COMMIT ?? "unknown"` in its onRemember callback (`src/pipeline/stages/execution.ts:27,119-139`); `_executionDeps` is the existing test seam (`src/pipeline/stages/execution.ts:304-317`). `NAX_COMMIT` is already exported at `src/version.ts:42`. Add the link factory to that dependency object and use the build constant without changing ask-chain order, approval-store shape, transport behavior, or existing audit flow. Future approval entries gain provenance; historic `unknown` records are intentionally not migrated.

Permissions are centrally resolved in `resolvePermissions`; its invalid-profile arm deliberately returns gated with no `toolGrants` (`src/config/permissions.ts:245-282`). `resolveBashSupport` only synthesizes Bash in raw and otherwise derives Bash availability from the same grant list (`src/agents/coding-tool-bash.ts:43-75`). The new detector must call that resolver for exactly four Bash-declaring stages, normalize an absent grant list to empty, and avoid package overrides and op-level narrowing. The config barrel currently exports only the PipelineStage type from permissions (`src/config/index.ts:17-18`). Setup currently invokes `warnFallbackMisconfiguration` once before credential validation (`src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts:145-150`); `run-setup-warnings.ts` establishes the optional logger and `_setup` warning-data convention (`src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-warnings.ts:68-98`). Add one sibling warning invocation at that seam. The `bashApproval` schema field is at `src/config/schemas-execution.ts:255-257` and needs documentation only. Risks are detector/tool-offer divergence, invalid profiles throwing, duplicate preflight warnings, source-size limits, and turning a valid no-shell posture into a failure; all changes must remain warning-only and backwards compatible.
outOfScope: nax#2194 (under `escalate`, Category B checks are skipped for ungranted or unlexable Bash commands) is not part of this feature; `checkBashCommand`'s evaluation order is unchanged.
US-001 only: `resolveWithin` in `src/tools/policy.ts` is not modified; typed tools must keep receiving `null` for nax config files.
US-001 only: the raw screen does not gain `.git/` protection or any containment check; `raw` enforces no root containment by design.
US-001 only: commands the lexer refuses (substitution, heredocs, backticks) stay unscreened; the screen is an advisory mistake-catcher, and the OS sandbox is what makes the guarantee airtight.
US-003 only: the warning reads the root run config only; per-package `.nax/mono/<pkg>/config.json` overrides of `bashApproval` or permissions are not inspected.
US-003 only: op-level `toolPatterns` narrowing is not considered; a stage is inert only when its resolved grants contain no `Bash` entry at all.
US-003 only: an inert stage is never turned into a config error or a run failure.
Tool-audit `approval.remembered` always being `false` is not part of this feature.
Tool-result truncation in `src/tools/bash.ts` (nax#2151) is not part of this feature.
